852-democracy-and-education-an-introduct.title: Democracy And Education An Introduction To The Philosophy Of
852-democracy-and-education-an-introduct.creator: John Dewey
852-democracy-and-education-an-introduct.description: A book by John Dewey. The most notable distinction between living and inanimate things is that the former maintain themselves by renewal. A stone when struck resists. If its resistance is greater than the force of the blow struck, it remains outwardly unchanged. Otherwise, it is shattered into smaller bits.

arxiv-2205-04798.title: Non-reciprocal Exciton-Polariton Ring Lattices
arxiv-2205-04798.creator: Huawen Xu, Kevin Dini, Xingran Xu, Rimi Banerjee, Subhaskar Mandal, Timothy C. H. Liew
arxiv-2205-04798.description: Abstract Recent experiments have shown the transfer of orbital angular momentum (OAM) from a non-resonant laser onto an exciton-polariton condensate, despite earlier views that the phase information of such a laser should be lost during the process of polariton condensation.

arxiv-2206-01466.title: Recognition of Unseen Bird Species by Learning from Field Guides
arxiv-2206-01466.creator: Andrés C. Rodríguez, Stefano D’Aronco, Rodrigo Caye Daudt, Jan D. Wegner, Konrad Schindler
arxiv-2206-01466.description: Abstract We exploit field guides to learn bird species recognition, in particular zero-shot recognition of unseen species. Illustrations contained in field guides deliberately focus on discriminative properties of each species, and can serve as side information to transfer knowledge from seen to unseen bird species.

arxiv-2206-02683.title: Mapping out the glassy landscape of a mesoscopic elastoplastic model
arxiv-2206-02683.creator: D. Kumar, S. Patinet, C. E. Maloney, I. Regev, D. Vandembroucq, M. Mungan
arxiv-2206-02683.description: Abstract We develop a mesoscopic model to study the plastic behavior of an amorphous material under cyclic loading. The model is depinning-like and driven by a disordered thresholds dynamics which are coupled by long-range elastic interactions. We propose a simple protocol of “glass preparation” which allows us to mimic thermalisation at high temperature, as well as aging at vanishing temperature.

arxiv-2212-05308.title: Controllability of periodic linear systems, the Poincaré sphere, and quasi-affine systems
arxiv-2212-05308.creator: Fritz Colonius Institut für Mathematik, Universität Augsburg, Augsburg, Germany, Alexandre J. Santana and Juliana Setti Departamento de Matemática, Universidade Estadual de Maringá Maringá, Brazil
arxiv-2212-05308.description: Abstract Abstract: For periodic linear control systems with bounded control range, an autonomized system is introduced by adding the phase to the state of the system. Here a unique control set (i.e., a maximal set of approximate controllability) with nonvoid interior exists. It is determined by the spectral subspaces of the homogeneous part which is a periodic linear differential equation.

arxiv-2401-02938.title: Fast and Effective Weight Update for Pruned Large Language Models
arxiv-2401-02938.creator: Vladimír Boža boza@fmph.uniba.sk
arxiv-2401-02938.description: Abstract Pruning large language models (LLMs) is a challenging task due to their enormous size. The primary difficulty is fine-tuning the model after pruning, which is needed to recover the lost performance caused by dropping weights. Recent approaches have either ignored fine-tuning entirely, focusing on efficient pruning criteria, or attempted layer-wise weight updates, preserving the behavior of each layer.

arxiv-2401-04446.title: How Dataflow Diagrams Impact Software Security Analysis: an Empirical Experiment
arxiv-2401-04446.creator: Simon Schneider 1 , Nicolás E. Díaz Ferreyra 1 , Pierre-Jean Quéval 2 , Georg Simhandl 2 , Uwe Zdun 2 , Riccardo Scandariato 1
arxiv-2401-04446.description: Abstract Models of software systems are used throughout the software development lifecycle. Dataflow diagrams (DFDs), in particular, are well-established resources for security analysis. Many techniques, such as threat modelling, are based on DFDs of the analysed application. However, their impact on the performance of analysts in a security analysis setting has not been explored before.

arxiv-2408-05417.title: Inner Radius and Energy Conditions of Dark Matter Halos Surrounding Schwarzschild Black Holes
arxiv-2408-05417.creator: Zibo Shen a,b, Anzhong Wang a, Shaoyu Yin c
arxiv-2408-05417.description: Abstract We study a class of analytic models for a dark matter halo surrounding a Schwarzschild black hole sitting at the center of a galaxy, with a variable inner radius r in r_{\text{in}} at which the density profile of the dark matter halo vanishes. We examine in detail how the three energy conditions are satisfied in such models.

arxiv-2412-21050.title: Parabolic gap theorems for the Yang-Mills energy
arxiv-2412-21050.creator: Anuk Dayaprema, Alex Waldron
arxiv-2412-21050.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Anuk Dayaprema, Alex Waldron. We prove parabolic versions of several known gap theorems in classical Yang-Mills theory. On an SU ⁡ ( r ) {\mathrm{SU}}(r) -bundle of charge κ \kappa over the 4-sphere, we show that the space of all connections with Yang-Mills energy less than 4 ​ π 2 ​ ( | κ | + 2 ) 4\pi^{2}\left(|\kappa|+2\right) deformation-retracts under Yang-Mills flow onto the space of instantons, allowing us to simplify the proof of Taubes’s path-connectedness theorem.

arxiv-2502-03009.title: Scaling Laws for Upcycling Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
arxiv-2502-03009.creator: Seng Pei Liew, Takuya Kato, Sho Takase
arxiv-2502-03009.description: Abstract Pretraining large language models (LLMs) is resource-intensive, often requiring months of training time even with high-end GPU clusters. There are two approaches of mitigating such computational demands: reusing smaller models to train larger ones (upcycling), and training computationally efficient models like mixture-of-experts (MoE).

arxiv-2507-00412.title: ViscoReg: Neural Signed Distance Functions via Viscosity Solutions
arxiv-2507-00412.creator: Meenakshi Krishnan, Ramani Duraiswami
arxiv-2507-00412.description: Abstract Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) that learn a Signed Distance Function (SDF) are a powerful tool for continuous 3D scene reconstruction. These models are trained by enforcing the Eikonal equation. We demonstrate theoretically that despite the ill-posedness of the Eikonal equation, generalization error estimates may be obtained for Neural SDFs in terms of the training error.

arxiv-2508-15457.title: Enhancing Novel View Synthesis from extremely sparse views with SfM-free 3D Gaussian Splatting Framework
arxiv-2508-15457.creator: Zongqi He, Hanmin Li, Kin-Chung Chan, Yushen Zuo, Hao Xie, Jun Xiao, Kin-Man Lam
arxiv-2508-15457.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zongqi He, Hanmin Li, Kin-Chung Chan, Yushen Zuo, Hao Xie, Jun Xiao, Kin-Man Lam. 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has demonstrated remarkable real-time performance in novel view synthesis, yet its effectiveness relies heavily on dense multi-view inputs with precisely known camera poses, which are rarely available in real-world scenarios. When input views become extremely sparse, the Structure-from-Motion (SfM) method that 3DGS depends on for initialization fails to accurately reconstruct the 3D geometric structures of scenes, resulting in degraded rendering quality.

arxiv-2511-20671.title: WiRainbow: Single-Antenna Direction-Aware Wi-Fi Sensing via Dispersion Effect Conference: The 30th Annual International Conference on Mobile Computing and Networking; May 11–14, 2026; Saint-Malo, France The 24th ACM/IEEE International Conference on Embedded Artificial Intelligence and Sensing System
arxiv-2511-20671.creator: Zhaoxin Chang 1∗ , Shuguang Xiao 2,3∗ , Fusang Zhang 4 , Xujun Ma 1 , Badii Jouaber 1 , Qingfeng Zhang 3# , Daqing Zhang 1,5#
arxiv-2511-20671.description: Abstract . Recently, Wi-Fi signals have emerged as a powerful tool for contactless sensing. During the sensing process, obtaining target direction information can provide valuable contextual insights for various applications. Existing direction estimation methods typically rely on antenna arrays, which are costly and complex to deploy in real-world scenarios.

arxiv-2601-21210.title: Uncovering Hidden Correctness in LLM Causal Reasoning via Symbolic Verification
arxiv-2601-21210.creator: Paul He, Yinya Huang, Mrinmaya Sachan, Zhijing Jin
arxiv-2601-21210.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being applied to tasks that involve causal reasoning. However, current benchmarks often rely on string matching or surface-level metrics that do not capture whether the output of a model is formally valid under the semantics of causal reasoning.
